liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (3 reviews): An ultra-light plane flew low over the crowd during Bird Song, which the crowd loved; Reviewer remembers a plane overhead, tied to the Bird Song moment, and traveled from Scotland for the shows [32][35][41]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Hissing noise appears in the second minute of Sugaree and then disappears [38]
- **A Touch of Gray** (1 review): Touch of Gray is described as solid, in contrast to its historically inconsistent performances [42]
- **Hey Pockey Way** (1 review): Hey Pocky Way showcased Brent's playing [42]

## Setlist highlights

- **let Mickey sing**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [44]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.morris.crazyfingers.106587.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.92586.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 149 min [2]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.92585.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.98647.dvda**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 0 min [8]
- **gd88-07-03.sbd.ststephen.3908.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min; rated 4.42/5 by 52 [22]. Said about its sound: Tapes are crystal clear with strong bass extension, though the bass is unruly on high-end stereos; Hissing occurs during the second minute of Sugaree, then stops; bass levels and Jerry's vocals sound good; Reviewer rates the sound excellent, A+ [32][38][42]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls a man climbing the huge fence while the crowd cheered him on [35]
- Oxford had been trashed the previous week by Monsters of Rock fans, so locals feared the Dead; fans left only footprints [39]
- Little Feat's opening set put the band in a good space; Bobby played a pink guitar [41]
- It was very hot; the band was helicoptered in because of traffic, and Jerry wore an ice outfit [43]
- A Looks Like Rain false start occurred after Touch of Gray [2]
- Reviewer has heard many recordings from the weekend and rates these among the best [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.morris.crazyfingers.106587.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; transferred by Chuck T.; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM-300 (CP-4) x2 > Cassette Master (Sony TCD5M/TDK MA 90) [1]
- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.92586.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Nakamichi CM-300's w/CP-4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby [2]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source by Carpenter; a patch from another ShnID covers a tape flip in I Will Take You Home [2]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.92585.flac16**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD (3908) + AUD (82801) + AUD (3325) [3]. Also: Matrix blend of soundboard and audience sources; missing between-song tuning and crowd noise was filled from audience tapes [3]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.98647.dvda**: taped by See Info file; transferred by Surround sound by Dan Haugh; source: DVD-Audio 5.1 Surround Sound (MLP Encoded 6ch x 16/44) [8]. Also: Audience source by Tony Suraci used Nakamichi CM304 mics, Beyer M101, Sony mixer and Sony D5M, stand at nine feet; Second audience source by Charlie Conner used Beyer Dynamic 201 mics into a Sony TCD5M, transferred via Nak DR-10 [8]
- **gd88-07-03.sbd.ststephen.3908.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [22]
